action: Check PostgreSQL, MySQL, Oracle Database and Oracle REST Data Services against the fixed versions in the vendor advisories and patch. Review which low-privilege database accounts exist.
date_note: Date the article was published; the researcher's exploits were released shortly before.
exec: Widely used databases have working proof-of-concept exploits that let low-privilege accounts run code on the server. Vendors have patched four of the flaws.
plain: A researcher published working code showing that a low-privilege database account can take over the server in PostgreSQL, MySQL and other databases. Most have fixes.

key_findings: Researcher Zheng Yu of Depthfirst published proofs of concept for memory-corruption bugs in PostgreSQL, MySQL and ClickHouse, plus an Oracle chain needing no login.
Four flaws have vendor CVEs and fixes; ClickHouse has no CVE and no confirmed fixed version.
The article says no attack in the wild has been seen and the full chains were not reproduced independently.

summary: The Hacker News reports that researcher Zheng Yu of Depthfirst published proof-of-concept exploits that let low-privilege database accounts run code on the server in PostgreSQL, MySQL and ClickHouse, plus an Oracle chain needing no login. Four flaws have CVEs and vendor fixes; ClickHouse has neither. No attacks in the wild are reported, and the chains were not independently reproduced.
title: Researcher publishes database RCE exploits for PostgreSQL, MySQL and Oracle
